title: Ulyana and the Wreck
premise: Ulyana Iversen has spent a decade flying medicine and mail across the interior, outrunning the memory of the wreck that killed her father and ended her first expedition. When her old rival Marcus Hale hires her crew to locate a downed survey plane, she realizes too late it is the same aircraft — and that her father's final flight carried something worth killing for: a mineral strike and a ledger proving Hale's family stole the claim. As sabotage, storms, and a stowaway journalist close in, Ulyana must choose between burying the truth to save the expedition or exposing it and losing everything she built. In the end she crashes deliberately to destroy the evidence, survives by trusting the rival who betrayed her, and returns home owning neither the secret nor the shame — only the sky.
about_author: Odile Kavanagh is a former flight dispatcher who spent six years in northern bush country before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels about people whose pasts are larger than their maps.

chapters.title: Fuel and Rumors
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A routine medicine run into a trapping camp introduces her world: the Beaver aircraft, the gossip network of the interior, and her careful avoidance of the eastern ranges where her father died. The beat is competence masking grief; she refuses a charter request without reading who sent it.

chapters.title: The Man at the Dock
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Marcus Hale arrives at her floatplane base offering triple rates to find a missing survey plane. She recognizes him from the expedition ten years ago and nearly throws him off the dock — until he mentions her father's name and a debt she can't ignore. Beat: old anger reignited into reluctant agreement.

chapters.title: Crew of Four
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Ulyana and her mechanic, Dez. They assemble the team: Dez, young pilot Teodora hungry for hours, and guide Sam Two-Rivers who was on the original expedition and says nothing. Beat: uneasy camaraderie; Sam's silence plants the first seed of dread.

chapters.title: Weather Window
chapters.summary: Teodora's POV. The flight east through deteriorating weather showcases Ulyana's skill and Hale's impatience. Teodora idolizes Ulyana but notices her hands shaking on the yoke near the pass. Beat: hero worship cracking as the mentor's fear becomes visible.

chapters.title: What the Lake Keeps
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Basecamp on the shore below the crash zone; sonar sweeps of the lake find nothing. At night Ulyana dreams of her father's last radio call. Hale privately checks a map he shouldn't have. Beat: the search feels staged — because parts of it are.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Sam's POV, first time inside his head. He reveals to the reader (not Ulyana) that he found the wreck years ago and took a waterproof ledger from it — a claim record implicating Hale's father in theft and fraud. Beat: guilt; he came along to finally give it back or burn it.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Someone drains fuel and cuts a tie-down overnight; the Beaver's float is holed. With one plane crippled, the expedition is stranded until repairs. Suspicion turns inward. Beat: paranoia replaces purpose; Ulyana realizes someone wanted them here and grounded.

chapters.title: The Stowaway
chapters.summary: Teodora's POV. They discover journalist Priya Raman hidden among the cargo drums — she traced Hale's permits and smells a story about the old strike. Ulyana wants her gone; there's no plane to send her in. Beat: an unwanted witness becomes an unavoidable variable.

chapters.title: Hale's Version
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Around the stove he tells his story: his father's obsession, the family's ruin, the letter claiming the wreck holds proof that could restore the Hale name — or end it. He admits he lied about the missing survey plane. Beat: sympathy earned, trust not yet given.

chapters.title: Ascent
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. With the float patched, they hike toward the ridgeline where the original wreck sits above the lake. Flashbacks braid with the climb: her father teaching her to read wind on rock. Beat: grief and purpose converging as the terrain grows familiar and terrible.

chapters.title: The Wreck
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. They reach the fuselage. Ulyana finds her father's remains undisturbed — and evidence someone else has been here recently, recently enough to leave boot prints over hers from years ago. Beat: devastation braided with the cold realization that the site has been visited, and watched.

chapters.title: Boot Prints
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. The prints match Hale's boots — but Hale swears he's never climbed here, and his boots don't fit the tread. Someone else is on the mountain: a claim-jumper hired by the company that profited from the theft. Beat: the enemy reframes; Hale becomes fellow quarry.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: Teodora's POV. Their satellite phone is dead — antenna cut. The stranger has cut them off deliberately. First snow squalls move in. Priya proves useful, rigging a spare antenna from salvage. Beat: isolation tightening; fragile alliances form around necessity.

chapters.title: What Her Father Carried
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In the wreck's strongbox: core samples of extraordinary ore and a second copy of the ledger, plus a letter addressed to Ulyana herself, written the night before the fatal flight. She reads it alone. Beat: the emotional core — her father knew the risk and chose her over the claim.

chapters.title: The Letter's Terms
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. Ulyana shows Sam the letter; he confesses he's held the ledger for ten years, unable to deliver or destroy it. Together they decide the strike must never be developed — this wilderness forgives nothing. Beat: two keepers of the secret finally sharing the weight.

chapters.title: The Stranger Descends
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. The claim-jumper, Voss, walks into camp armed and polite, offering to buy everyone's silence. Hale recognizes him as his father's old fixer. Negotiation curdles into threat when Voss demands the strongbox contents. Beat: open confrontation; the stakes turn mortal.

chapters.title: Storm Line
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A full storm pins everyone at the wreck site through a whiteout night. Voss tries to take the samples; Sam stops him and takes a beating. Ulyana hides the ledger in the one place no one will look — inside her father's grave cairn. Beat: sacrifice and resolve hardened into decision.

chapters.title: Descent and Deception
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. They fake the strongbox's destruction, scattering ore samples in the lake while Voss watches from the ridge. The repaired Beaver can lift only four plus fuel — someone must stay. Ulyana volunteers, planning to wait out the storm and walk out. Beat: leadership as self-erasure.

chapters.title: Voss's Mistake
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. On the flight out, Voss forces his way aboard at gunpoint, demanding they fly him to the company's staging strip. Teodora, flying, must outthink a hijacker with a storm on the nose. Beat: terror in the cockpit; the apprentice becomes the pilot her mentor made.

chapters.title: Controlled Descent
chapters.summary: Teodora's POV, climax part one. Teodora feigns engine failure and puts the Beaver down hard on a frozen bay, disabling it and breaking Voss's arm in the crash. Everyone survives. Beat: cathartic climax — skill, nerve, and the crew's trust defeating brute force.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, climax part two. Rescued and grounded, Ulyana gives Priya the whole story on record — the theft, the ledger, the cover-up — then surrenders the ledger's location to authorities rather than bury it. Hale chooses testimony over his family name. Beat: truth chosen over safety; identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Long Way Home
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, resolution. Weeks later, the investigation underway and the ranges closed to claims, Ulyana flies medicine runs again — with Teodora as her new co-pilot and Sam fishing off her dock. She visits the cairn one last time and leaves the letter there. Beat: belonging found not in the past recovered, but in the life flown forward.
